title: Attention training in multiple sclerosis
description: Many people with multiple sclerosis have problems with attention and concentration. Cognitive rehabilitation trains these skills with structured exercises. In one small randomised trial, people who did intensive computer-based attention training did better on an attention test than people who did a placebo programme, and this went with more activity at the back of the cerebellum and at the top of the parietal lobe. In this episode brightness shows more activity after training compared with the placebo group.
caveat: All findings come from one trial of 23 people with multiple sclerosis and attention problems: 12 did the training and 11 a placebo programme. Only the abstract could be read; it compares the groups after training and does not say whether the brain was scanned before training as well, nor whether the activity was a group difference or a link with how much attention improved. The posterior cerebellar lobule is drawn on the cerebellum outline, an approximation, and the superior parietal lobule is not in the brain model. Lesions were not measured in this study. These are averages across groups of people, not a picture of any one person's brain. Treatments help many people, not everyone, and in different ways. This is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or therapist about what is right for you.

citations.title: Computer-assisted cognitive rehabilitation of attention deficits for multiple sclerosis: a randomized trial with fMRI correlates.
citations.quote: Using a double-blind randomized controlled study, we enrolled 12 MS patients, who underwent a CR program (experimental group), and 11 age-gender-matched MS patients, who underwent a placebo intervention (control group).

phases.caption: After training, attention was better than in the placebo group, and this went with more activity at the back of the cerebellum and in the superior parietal lobule during an attention task.

regions.explanation: The posterior cerebellar lobule was more active during an attention task after intensive attention training, compared with a placebo programme, in one trial of 23 people with multiple sclerosis. The abstract does not make clear whether this is a group difference or a link with how much attention improved. Drawn on the cerebellum outline, an approximation.

citations.title: Computer-assisted cognitive rehabilitation of attention deficits for multiple sclerosis: a randomized trial with fMRI correlates.
citations.quote: After CR, the experimental group, in comparison with the control group, showed a specific enhanced performance in attention abilities as assessed by the Stroop task with an effect size of 0.88, which was associated with increased activity in the posterior cerebellar lobule and in the superior parietal lobule.
